main_body: A 4x3-tile ground patch of brick-like paving in beige and pink-brown, with dark grey mortar lines and a few blue-grey and dark-green strip patches. It is a flat surface, not a standing object.
top_band: none. This is a flat terrain surface, so there is no standing volume and no top-versus-front split to read in a pixel column.
evidence: The kind is terrain (a ground paving patch), so the 3/4 standing-object contract does not apply. The brick rows tile as a floor surface with no standing body, no side faces and no elevation drawing. Nothing in Part A fails.

style.evidence: The bricks use about 4 steps (light beige, beige, pink-brown, dark grey mortar). The beige brick faces are flat fills of roughly 8x3 px or more, with only sparse dots of grain. The mortar is a neutral dark grey with almost no tint, which reads as a near-black sticker line rather than a dark tone of the neighbouring material. Blue-grey blocks and dark bars with grey fragments at the top edge and in a few spots look like stray artifacts rather than deliberate shading. The Beodeul paving reference shades each stone individually with 5-6 steps and carries far more colours per tile. This candidate's tiles are mostly 3-4 colours, so it looks thinner and flatter next to the reference.
